heading: Predicted per capita GDP in the production model
cell_title: Website version: Fig. 4 with a precomputed slider for the year ("Other countries" in the legend)
plot_title: 2023: China has 35% of U.S. capital per person, predicted income 71%
source_note:
**Sources.** Data: [Penn World Table 11.0](https://www.rug.nl/ggdc/productivity/pwt/), Groningen Growth and Development Centre ([DOI 10.34894/FABVLR](https://doi.org/10.34894/FABVLR)), variables `rgdpo` (real GDP), `pop` (population) and `csh_i` (investment share); cite as Feenstra, Inklaar and Timmer (2015), ["The Next Generation of the Penn World Table"](https://doi.org/10.1257/aer.20130954), *American Economic Review* 105(10). Capital per person is our own perpetual-inventory estimate from PWT investment, and TFP is computed from it. The curve is the model's prediction, $y^* = k^{1/3}$.
Prepared file: [`data/ch04/pwt_production.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch04/pwt_production.csv) (see the [data notes](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch04/README.md)).
Chart: inspired by Fig. 4.4 in Jones (2024), [*Macroeconomics*, 6th ed.](https://wwnorton.com/books/9781324063612)
